title: A Large-Scale Empirical Study on Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Unit Testing
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
datasets: Methods2Test_filter (56,132 pairs) + Defects4J (163 bug instances / five projects) for test generation; Data_old (156,760) for assertions; 5,196 test evolution samples; private industrial validation set.
models: 37 open code LLMs and six instruction-tuned prompt models; best D4J correct-test models DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B and CodeLlama-7B; prompt baseline GPT-3.5
license: Paper CC BY 4.0; repository README says MIT but referenced LICENSE is missing/404
input_setting: Method→test, focal/test-without-assert→assertion, old/new method+old test→updated test
reproduction_grade: B- (conditional due compute, missing TestGen dataset/checkpoints and hard-coded D4J paths)
limitation: Full study consumes >3,000 A100 hours; no fine-tuned checkpoints and filtered Methods2Test data not in repository. D4J bug detection best is only 8/163, .74% precision; no root-cause taxonomy.
task: Empirical fine-tuning study across test generation, assertion generation, test evolution; separate bug detection on Defects4J
